title: The carrier Junyō, 9 December 1944
eyebrow: South-west of Nagasaki · SEA DEVIL's, PLAICE's and REDFISH's patrols

participants.name: Junyō
participants.note: returning from Mako to the home islands (the Imperial Navy's summary); SEA DEVIL's radar had one very large pip, two large and four small, the task force never sighted; REDFISH took her for a SHOKAKU or HAYATAKA type carrier

participants.name: Maki
participants.note: a destroyer of the screen (Matsu class); the Imperial Navy's summary has her hit once in the bow, back at Nagasaki at 1000; PLAICE took the screen for TERUTSUKI class; the silhouette is the kit's generic destroyer

paras.text: Three boats on one carrier's force in the night of 8–9 December 1944: SEA DEVIL's four stern torpedoes at 0028 I, PLAICE's salvoes at the screen at 0128 and 0131 I, and REDFISH's attacks at 0156 and 0320 I, as typed on their attack sheets, beside the Imperial Navy's summary, which has Junyō torpedoed once, two hits, at 0130, and the destroyer Maki hit in the bow.

Junyō, returning from Mako, was torpedoed about 50 miles south-west of Nomozaki: two hits, but she could make 13 knots on one shaft and entered Sasebo about 1000 (p. 5) [[cite:jacar:C16120660300]]. The same page has the destroyer Maki hit once in the bow, 30 miles from Meshima, and back at Nagasaki at 1000, entered at 0200 in a block whose day is not marked. The summary does not say whose torpedoes. Three boats' records can be set against it:

- SEA DEVIL timed two explosions at 0031:40 and 0031:55 I, each checking with a torpedo's run; PLAICE heard three at 0030 by her own clock, "established ... as hits from the SEA DEVIL's attack". Two hits, as the summary has, an hour before its time. - PLAICE fired three bow torpedoes at the leading destroyer at 0128 I, saw "a large carrier with island superstructure" come out of a rain squall at 0129, heard two hits in the destroyer at 0131, fired four stern torpedoes diving at the third destroyer, and heard two more hits at 0133. Her hits fit the summary's time; her targets, as she saw them, were the screen. - REDFISH claimed one hit at 0156 I and one more at 0320 I nearer Nomozaki.
Every pairing is possible: which boat hit Junyō, and which Maki, is open until a record with their own times is found.
Positions are each boat's own; lines between them are straight. Junyō is drawn from the boats' sightings, and no Japanese position is given in figures.

SEA DEVIL's and PLAICE's sheets type zone I; REDFISH's Attack 7 sheet types a J that is read here as I (the reason is given with her attack, under Questions and sources). Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9).

Junyō's own record and her escorts' December diaries: none found on JACAR by her name or the 21st Destroyer Division's. SEA POACHER and PIRANHA were in the area that night (SEA DEVIL's ship contacts) and are not in the kit.

War patrol reports, NARA microfilm M1752: SEA DEVIL Patrol 2 (74843922), PLAICE Patrol 3 (74832413), REDFISH Patrol 2 (74837267). The Navy's day-by-day summary of escort and anti-submarine events, December 1944, via JACAR (C16120660300, National Institute for Defense Studies). Coastline: Natural Earth.

outcome.note: Junyō torpedoed, two hits, at 0130 I. SEA DEVIL's two explosions (0031:40 and 0031:55 I) each checked with a torpedo's run, and PLAICE heard them at 0030 I by her own clock and signalled that she saw the hits (ss-390-plaice/3, Attack 1's note): two hits, as the summary has, but an hour before its time. REDFISH's Attack 7 (0156 I) claimed one hit. Possible, until a record with Junyō's own times is found (her escorts' or Sasebo's December diaries)

outcome.note: PLAICE heard two hits in the leading destroyer at 0131 I and breaking-up noises for four minutes. The summary has Maki hit once in the bow at 0200 (J02, its day inferred), about 20 nm from PLAICE's position; Maki reached Nagasaki, so did not sink. The time is half an hour after the hits and the count one against two

Junyō's two hits are timed 0130 I (J01), between PLAICE's firing at 0128 and the hits she heard at 0131; she saw the carrier at 0129, just after firing at the leading destroyer. SEA DEVIL's two hits (0031:40 and 0031:55 I, which PLAICE heard at 0030) came an hour before the summary's time; REDFISH's (0156 I) 26 minutes after

outcome.note: REDFISH claimed one hit on a SHOKAKU or HAYATAKA type carrier at 0156 (31-57N 129-01E). The summary records Junyō torpedoed about 50 miles south-west of Nomozaki, which fits that position, with two hits, at 0130 I. Its one time is 26 minutes before Attack 7 by REDFISH's zone I (or 34 minutes after, if the J the sheet types is right). SEA DEVIL's report (ss-400-sea-devil/2, Attack 4) times two explosions at 0031:40 and 0031:55 I at 31-43N 129-04E, each checking with a torpedo's run, and PLAICE saw her hits: two hits, as the summary has, an hour before its 0130. PLAICE (ss-390-plaice/3) heard her own hits at 0131 and 0133 I on what she took for destroyers of the screen, at 31-57N 129-01E, the position REDFISH's sheet types for this attack; the summary also has the destroyer Maki hit in the bow. Its place (about 50 miles south-west of Nomozaki) is nearer REDFISH's and PLAICE's. Which boat's torpedoes made the two hits the summary does not say

words.type_attack: Night radar submerged approach. Dropped to periscope depth to let escorts by and tracked target by sound bearings from JP-2 and JK equipment. Fired by T.D.C. and spread by offset handle with radar bearings and ranges.
words.description: Contact was made by radar at range of 33,000 yards. The radar screen showed one very large pip, two large pips and four small pips at 28,000 yards. The night was overcast with poor visibility resulting in the task force never being sighted.
words.damaged: One large warship. Probably BB or CV.
words.determined_by: Two explosions timed exactly with the generated torpedo run to be torpedo hits in the target. A third explosion was heard that did not check with torpedo run to this target. Received a message from U.S.S. PLAICE saying they saw our hits.
words.target_line: Target Draft: 28 feet Course: 050°T Speed: 19 knots Range: 4315 yds.
words.own_ship: Speed: 4 knots Course: 161°T Depth: 42 feet Angle: 3° down
words.note: Tube 10 typed "Miss (?)". The narrative (p10-p11) times the attack to the second: 0005 dived to radar depth; 0027 commenced firing four Mk 23s from the stern tubes, range 4300 yards, 115° starboard track, depth set 6 feet, gyros 180°, "Although the torpedo runs were around 5000 yards, this was our only shot"; fired #7 0027:45, #8 0028:00, #9 0028:18, #10 0028:28; explosions 0031:40 ("checked exactly with #8 torpedo") and 0031:55 (#9); 0033:05 one explosion, unknown; 0035 pinging and screws close aboard, went deep; 0050 screws faded out. The sheet's intervals (10 sec.) round the narrative's 15, 18 and 10 seconds

words.description: Task Force consisting of one SHOKAKU or HAYATAKA type aircraft carrier, one battleship, three escorting destroyers. The aircraft carrier was attacked. Initial contact was by SJ Radar range 31,000 yards. Visibility at time of attack about 6,000 yds.
words.damaged: (EC) Damaged one SHOKAKU or HAYATAKA type aircraft carrier (29,800 tons).
words.determined_by: Commanding Officer on bridge observed one timed hit (2min. 10 sec) after commenced firing.
words.remarks: * At least one of these torpedoes ran erratic as determined by sound bearings after firing. It is not known which one. Unable to explain other misses. Course 050T. and speed 13 were used in estimate of course and speed. Plotting of definitely observed timed hit shows course 070T. speed 11. It is believed target was employing a modified constant helm zig plan.

words.type_attack: Night surface attack against task force. Density of the screen effectively prevented penetration. Visibility ruled out a submerged attack. Fired 3 bow tubes on radar ranges and bearings for two correctly timed hits. The next destroyer astern turned toward, spoiling the set-up for the remainder of the bow nest. See Attack No. 2 for continuation with the stern tubes.
words.description: Task Force of 2 large ships and 6 small ones by radar. Sighted one large aircraft carrier (SHOKAKU Class (EU)) and 2 destroyers (TERUTSUKI Class 1 (EC) and 1 (EU)). The two large ships were in line abreast with an estimated 3 destroyers in column 3,000 yards on each flank. The last quarter moon was obscured by clouds and intermittent rain squalls. Target not seen until just before firing.
words.damaged: One fleet type destroyer, TERUTSUKI Class (EC).
words.determined_by: Heard two correctly timed hits. Heard loud and definite breaking up noises for four minutes.

Decided our best chance lies in a divided bow nest salvo at the two leading destroyers and a stern nest salvo at the big boy during the ensuing confusion"; 0128 fired #1, #2 and #3 at the leading destroyer; 0129 "The big boy popped out of the rain squall. He was a large carrier with island superstructure"; 0131 "Heard two hits in the leading destroyer while diving". At 0030 she had "Heard three explosions below decks, which sounded like torpedo hits. Later information established these as hits from the SEA DEVIL's attack" (p11)

words.type_attack: This attack was actually a continuation of Torpedo Attack Number One. When the second destroyer turned toward us, shifted the set-up from that one with bow tubes to the third one in line with stern tubes. Commenced firing about 30 seconds after the diving alarm sounded while avoiding what looked like an attempt to ram. The first shot went out on a radar range and bearing. The next three were fired on generated bearings.
